method: Individual review of 16 pending expressions and targeted additions for source barriers. Distressing quotations remain attributed; no abusive procedures or treatment advice are added to teaching examples.
phrases: been around
existed or been present for some time
存在一段时间了
That shop has been around for decades.
那家店已经开了几十年。
Be around can mean be nearby, but here it concerns longevity; the previous founding date provides the time context.
has been there since
has existed or remained in that place from a starting time until the reference time
自……以来一直在那里
The library has been there since 1985.
那座图书馆自1985年以来一直在那里。
Since introduces a starting point, not a duration; contrast for many years. Teaching date is invented for the example, not a correction of the source date.
on the precipice of
very close to a major transition, often with a sense of risk
处于……的边缘；即将进入……阶段
The company was on the precipice of a major change.
公司即将迎来一次重大变化。
Figurative cliff-edge image with of + noun/-ing. Source trails off at becoming a and continues in 340; do not treat 339 as a complete model sentence.
the night of
the night associated with a specified date or event
……的那一晚
We stayed nearby the night of the concert.
演唱会那晚我们住在附近。
Of introduces the event or date, not duration. Source links the night to initiation, without providing a new timestamp.
all over
across many parts or the whole surface of something
到处；遍布……
There were sticky notes all over the desk.
桌子上到处都是便签。
Distribution sense here, not all over meaning finished. Neutral teaching example is separate from the quoted allegation.
as it turned out
as was discovered later
后来发现；结果却是
As it turned out, the spare key was in my bag.
后来发现，备用钥匙就在我的包里。
Introduces hindsight, often contrary to expectation. Source reveals the reported riddle had no answer.
for the first time
on an occasion when something had never happened before
第一次
She spoke at a conference for the first time.
她第一次在会议上发言。
Use for with first-time occurrence. Reviewing the time phrase does not resolve the nonstandard essayed in the source.
no actual answer
no real or valid solution
没有真正的答案
The trick question had no actual answer.
那个捉弄人的问题没有真正的答案。
Actual means real, not current. Source asserts the riddle lacked a solution; it does not mean the person merely failed to solve it.
has been shut down
has been closed or stopped from operating
已经被关闭或停止运作
The old booking service has been shut down.
旧的预订服务已经停止运作。
Present-perfect passive, describing a closure relevant at the reference time. Narrated since 2024 is not independently checked as a current status.
shut down
close or stop operating an organization, service or system
关闭；停止运作
They shut down the service for maintenance.
他们关闭服务进行维护。
Can be transitive or intransitive; with a pronoun use shut it down. Does not necessarily mean a building was demolished.
worth reading
valuable enough to spend time reading
值得一读
The guide is short and worth reading.
这份指南简短，值得一读。
Worth takes -ing, not to read. Source recommendation does not certify the text as unbiased or error-free.
when he was a freshman
during his first year at a school or college
他还是一年级学生时
He joined the club when he was a freshman.
他还是一年级学生时就加入了那个社团。
Freshman is a first-year student in this college context, not a new employee generally. Teaching example is not a source quotation.
had endured months of
had suffered or put up with something for several months before a later past point
此前已忍受了数月的……
They had endured months of disruption before the repairs ended.
维修结束之前，他们已经忍受了数月的干扰。
Past perfect locates the suffering before the narrated moment; months of introduces duration plus a noun describing what was endured.
on my elbows and knees
with body weight supported on the elbows and knees
用我的手肘和膝盖支撑着身体
I was on my elbows and knees looking under the sofa.
我用手肘和膝盖撑着身体，往沙发下面看。
A posture phrase, not an instruction to reproduce the alleged forced action. Possessive pronouns change with the speaker.
unable to articulate
not able to express an idea or feeling clearly in words
无法清楚表达
She felt upset but was unable to articulate why.
她感到难过，却说不清为什么。
Articulate means put into words here, not move a mechanical joint. Lack of words does not mean lack of distress.
years ago
several years before the relevant present time
多年前
I visited that town years ago.
我多年前去过那个小城。
Ago normally accompanies past tense and is relative to the speaker's time. Do not replace the recording-relative date with today's date.
recounts
tells the details of a past event or experience
叙述；回忆讲述
The article recounts her first year at work.
文章讲述了她工作的第一年。
Reporting verb, not recalculating a number. Recounting an experience attributes an account rather than independently proving each detail.
Fully fledged
fully developed or having complete membership or status
完全成熟的；具备正式资格的
The prototype became a fully fledged product.
原型变成了一个成熟的产品。
Usually fully fledged before a noun; source then says fully pledged, a correction or wordplay tied to fraternity pledging. Preserve both original forms.
consisted of
was made up of the listed components
由……组成
The presentation consisted of three short sections.
演示由三个简短部分组成。
Consist of is not normally passive: consisted of, not was consisted of. Teaching example avoids turning the abusive mixture description into a recipe.
screamed bloody murder
screamed extremely loudly, especially in fear, pain or protest
拼命尖叫；大声惨叫
The character screamed bloody murder when the alarm startled him.
警报把那个角色吓了一跳，他拼命尖叫起来。
Idiomatic intensity, not an assertion that a murder occurred. Source describes reported distress; fictional neutral context is clearly a teaching example.
made to crawl
forced to move on hands and knees or with the body close to the ground
被迫爬行
The novel describes people being made to crawl through a narrow passage.
小说描写了人们被迫爬过一条狭窄通道。
Passive made to + verb expresses compulsion; active make someone crawl has no to. Source's missing was is retained, not silently repaired in the quotation.
collapsed
fell down suddenly because the body could no longer stay upright
突然倒下；瘫倒
The exhausted character collapsed beside the door.
那个筋疲力尽的角色倒在门旁。
Physical sense in source, not a company failing or a menu closing. No medical cause or diagnosis is inferred.
a whole piece
an entire article or written account in this context
一整篇文章或报道
There's a whole piece about the project in the local paper.
当地报纸有一整篇文章介绍这个项目。
Piece is a written work, not a physical fragment. Cornell Sun is the named publication, and recently is recording-relative.
liquor bottles
bottles containing or previously containing distilled alcoholic drinks
烈酒瓶
The recycling bin contained empty liquor bottles.
回收箱里有空的烈酒瓶。
American liquor usually means spirits, distinct from beer and wine. Presence of bottles alone does not prove who drank their contents.
segments: The reporting verb is now explicitly taught as telling a past experience; the hazing account remains attributed rather than independently verified.
Fully fledged denotes complete status, followed by a source correction or wordplay fully pledged. The phrase continues becoming a from 339 and is not silently standardized into one quoted form.
Compulsory passive action, crawl movement and body-support posture are explicitly explained. The source omits was before made; teaching grammar is separated from the preserved quote.
The physical sudden-fall sense is taught without inventing a cause, diagnosis or unreported action.
Piece is identified as an article and the named publication is recognized; which was published recently attaches to the article and uses recording-relative time.
Beer versus distilled spirits is explicitly distinguished; there's with a plural list is retained as spoken agreement, not taught as careful written grammar.
